veranderings.rede: Two instances of 'hulle' in one sentence point to different things (the pumpkin leaves, then 'baie blare'); naming the first removes the ambiguity, and the protected wording stays intact.

veranderings.voor: Dit gee die energie wat die plant vir die werk nodig het en wat gewoonlik van sonlig kom.
veranderings.na: Dit gee die energie wat die plant vir die werk nodig het. Hierdie lig is gewoonlik sonlig.
veranderings.rede: As written, the light gives energy 'that comes from sunlight', which reads as circular; splitting it says plainly that the light is usually sunlight, and keeps 'gewoonlik'.

veranderings.voor: Hulle bêre dit ook in hulle wortels en blomme, en in hulle vrugte en sade.
veranderings.na: Hulle bêre dit ook in hulle wortels, blomme, vrugte en sade.
veranderings.rede: AWS: no comma before 'en' between parts of one sentence; a single list is also smoother than the repeated 'in hulle'.

veranderings.voor: groei op die stysel in die saad
veranderings.na: gebruik die stysel in die saad om te groei
veranderings.rede: 'groei op' calques English 'grows on' and can be read as growing on top of the starch.
Leaves 'oopvou' is the natural Afrikaans verb for new leaves unfolding.

veranderings.blok: Stysel in die kos wat ons eet
veranderings.voor: kan wel stysel bevat as mense dit bygevoeg het
veranderings.na: kan wel stysel bevat wat mense bygevoeg het
veranderings.rede: 'dit' can be read as the sausage rather than the starch; a relative clause makes clear it is the starch that was added.
